Subject: Post-call: inference tooling comparison & next tests

Hi Jordan — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of call:
- Acme is evaluating inference providers for low-latency robotics teleops and on-device orchestration (hard SLOs: p99 < 120ms for 512 tokens).
- You plan to run a competitive eval vs hyperscaler hosted endpoints (Bedrock/Vertex) + one behind an internal proxy.
- Primary concerns: latency tail, predictable unit cost, and observability across model/route.

Open items we agreed to validate in the pilot:
1) Latency & cost head-to-head (p50/p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens)
2) Tracing + per-request annotations across model variants
3) Live dashboards for token-level cost and route-level error rates
4) Fallback behavior under capacity pressure (how our routing degrades to smaller variants)

Attachments: redwood-comparison-deck.pdf (summary & proposed test plan)

Proposed test plan (high level):
- 2x model classes: Llama2-70B quantized variant, and a mid-size open LLM (7B)
- Workload: 512-token prompts, mixed completion/profiled inference, repeatable test harness we provide
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, TPS, cost/1k tokens, KV cache hit rate, error rate
- Observability: we’ll enable request tracing and expose a per-route dashboard link (screenshot attached)

Next steps:
- Jordan: share sample test dataset or S3 access (+ any IP constraints) by EOD Friday
- Redwood (Neha + Rafael): schedule a 2-hour run window next week and provide a dedicated test key with tracing enabled
- Both: agree on the hyperscaler variants to include (Jordan suggested Bedrock + OpenAI)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with calendar options and the measurement template.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>

Hi Jordan — quick technical follow-up and concrete test configuration we’ve used successfully in similar evaluations. I’ll be hands-on during the run.

Short answers:
- Yes, we can run the same request stream and provide deterministic load (same seed, same inter-arrival distribution).
- Fallback rules: by default we route to the pinned primary model variant; on queue-growth or p95 latency breach we automatically route to a compatible quantized variant in the same family. We can make this conservative (notify-only) for the initial run.
- Dashboards: we provide managed per-route dashboards in Redwood Console and can export alerts/metrics to Datadog/Prometheus via metrics endpoint. Grafana can be wired to the metrics export.

Proposed test config (attach: test-config-sample.yaml):
- Models to include: rwdm-70b-q4f (primary), rwdm-7b-q4f (fallback), bedrock-special-70b, openai-gpt-4o-mini (for cost baseline)
- Payload: 512-token prompts, 1,000 unique prompts, 3 repeats each (total 3k requests)
- Concurrency profile: ramp 0→200 qps over 5m, hold 20m, cool-down 5m
- Instrumentation: attach header X-Request-ID + trace sampling=100% for the run; include per-request annotations (robot_id, route)
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, request CPU/GPU utilization, tokens/sec per GPU, cache hit rate, cost/1k tokens

Sample curl (redwood):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TEST_KEY>"
  -H "X-Request-ID: {{id}}"
  -d '{"model":"rwdm-70b-q4f","input":"<prompt>","max_tokens":512}'

Operational notes:
- We’ll enable real-time tracing in the Console; Rafael will share the dashboard link and a PNG screenshot (attached).
- For fairness, please run Bedrock/OpenAI with equivalent sequence length and repetition; we’ll provide the harness repository so both sides use the same client.

Next: Rafael and I will provision the test key and schedule the run slots (block of 2 hours). Vanessa — I’m copying Rafael on the dashboards/credentials.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.ai
